title: Core 2: Data Science Core
text:
CORE 2, DATA SCIENCE – NARRATIVE
The Data Science Core serves as a comprehensive, multi-disciplinary resource of expertise in biostatistics
and bioinformatics to assist investigators from all projects to design their experiments, manage and maintain
the large volume of data, make inference regarding the stated aims, and formulate new hypotheses based on
discoveries arising from exploration and visualization of the integrated data.

title: Deciphering microbial-immune cell interaction using single cell approaches
text:
Analyzing the transcriptional profiles of single microbial and innate immune cells during their interaction can lead
to better understanding of how one influences the other in a direct and indirect manner. This information can
provide mechanistic insights on how microbes and innate immune system co-evolve over time. This proposal is
centered on the optimization and use of a microfluidic single cell sequencing platform to unravel this interaction
which can eventually help understand the underlying mechanism of the maintenance and disruption of microbe-
immune system symbiosis.

title: Engineering a multi-targeted nanoparticle-based immunotherapy for pancreatic cancer
text:
Pancreatic cancer arises within an immune suppressive tumor microenvironment that limits anti-tumor immunity,
drug delivery, and the efficacy of immune checkpoint blockade (ICB) therapy that has demonstrated remarkable
success in other cancer types. We have recently shown that combinations of RAS pathway inhibitors targeting
oncogenic signaling in pancreatic tumors and innate immune agonists loaded into nanoparticles (NPs) can
synergistically target multiple mechanisms of immune suppression and activate cytotoxic T cell immunity in
PDAC. This proposal aims to engineer tumor and immune targeting therapies in NPs to specifically deliver them
to the PDAC microenvironment with minimal toxicity and evaluate their impact on anti-tumor immune responses
and ICB outcomes, with the goal of developing a novel immunotherapy regimen for lethal pancreatic cancer that
still remains without effective treatment options.

title: Reverse translation of human brain imaging data in mouse models of AUD
text: Abstract/Summary: Alcohol use disorder is a complex group of disorders involving excessive uncontrolled alcohol intake. Our recent human imaging data suggest distinct circuits of interest in male and female AUD subjects during abstinence. In this proposal, we will explore the insula-BNST circuit in female mice, testing whether negative affective disturbances that emerge during abstinence are associated with the relative strength of this pathway. We will further assess the therapeutic potential of the endocannabinoid system at this synapse by utilizing a novel genetic strategy of deletion of the CB1 cannabinoid receptor and the endocannabinoid 2-AG synthetic enzyme DAG lipase in patterns to determine its specific contribution to AUD-related behaviors at the insula- BNST synapse. In male mice, we will explore the disruption of the ventral hippocampal-BNST-hypothalamic circuit suggested by human imaging data in a model of operant alcohol seeking behavior. Finally, we will perform novel tracing strategies to determine afferent inputs to these pathways to inform future human imaging studies.

title: Elucidating the Role of Lactate in Immune Dysfunction during Sepsis: A Focus on B Cell Modulation
text:
Substantial evidence indicates that immune paralysis is a major driving force for mortality of sepsis. Sepsis
survivors usually develop long-lasting immunosuppressive state, rendering them more susceptible to
secondary infections. This R01 research project is highly relevant to public health as it aims to elucidate the
novel role of lactate in promoting the immunosuppression via regulating the numerical, phenotypic, and
functional changes in B cells following sepsis. The application also highlights B cell-derived GABA as a novel
mediator in sepsis-associated immune paralysis. Successful completion of this project will not only provide
insights into the cellular and molecular mechanisms of sepsis-associated immunosuppression but also
emphasize the potential of targeting lactate-associated signaling and identifying novel biomarkers (such as B
cell-derived GABA) to manage sepsis and septic shock.

title: T cell Contributions to Neointima Formation in Pulmonary Hypertension
text:
Pulmonary hypertension (PH) is a debilitating lung disease without cure that occurs both in isolation and as a
complication of conditions that range from autoimmune disease to congenital heart disease. This study will focus
on how perivascular T cells contribute to the development of PH by interrogating the T cell subtypes and ligands
associated with PH vascular lesion formation. The results will provide deeper insight into how the adaptive
immune system shapes lung vascular changes, and may help identify fundamental, therapeutically targetable
signaling pathways in PH or PH-associated lung diseases.

title: Therapeutic targeting of RTK protein granules in cancer
text:
Gene rearrangements involving receptor tyrosine kinases (RTKs) represent a frequent and diverse set of
oncogenic driver alterations across human cancer, and resistance to tyrosine kinase inhibitor (TKI) therapies
are inevitable for most patients with advanced cancers and the major cause of mortality. We recently
discovered that notable RTK fusion oncoproteins form their own pathogenic subcellular compartment,
membraneless cytoplasmic RTK protein granules, to coordinate oncogenic RTK and RAS signaling. This
proposal will test therapeutic approaches that exploit the unique signaling properties of this cancer-specific
biomolecular condensate.

title: RNA Nanosystem for Posterior Eye Drug Delivery
text:
Posterior eye diseases affect more than a million people in the United States each year. The present project
will develop an ocular drug delivery system based on RNA technology to deliver nucleotide-based drugs into
the eye to treat posterior eye diseases. It will be a great benefit to the public if an effective drug delivery system
can replace repeated intravitreal injections and allow effective nucleotide-based drug delivery for the
treatments of these diseases.

title: Targeting SEC61 complex to overcome resistance to immunotherapy in GBM
text:
Glioblastoma (GBM) is an incurable cancer with a dismal survival rate. Despite the promise of
immunotherapy in extracranial cancers, the clinical efficacy of immunotherapy has yet to be shown for GBM.
The unbiased genomic screen identified the gene encoding for the SEC61G subunit of translocon complex as a
gene involved in therapeutic resistance to T cells mediated therapy in GBM. This study will focus on
understanding the mechanisms underlying SEC61G-mediated immunotherapeutic resistance, validating the
SEC61G as a therapeutic target to improve poor outcomes in patients with GBM.

title: Core C- BIDMC Core
text:
Core C will ensure streamlined data generation, acquisition, quality control, management, and provenance
across the PPG. It will generate production-grade highly automated single cell and spatial tissue profiling data;
establish streamlined data processing, quality control, management, and provenance; as well as promote best
practice, scalable, multi-modal data processing, analysis, and integration. Core C will work closely with the
personnel of the Administrative Core, the Cores, and the Projects for efficient and timely data delivery.

title: Functional consequences of high glucose culture on adoptive T cell therapies for cancer
text:
A critical component of adoptive cell therapies for cancer treatment is the in vitro expansion step where T cells
are cultured in media containing very high levels of glucose to enhance proliferation. It has been well
demonstrated that the culture media used during in vitro expansion can imprint lasting effects on T cell effector
function in the tumor microenvironment, yet the mechanism by which high levels of glucose in culture media
alter T cell glycosylation remain understudied. This proposal aims to understand how exposure to high levels of
glucose, a clinical standard in the preparation of T cell therapies, alters therapeutic T cell effector function and
antitumor immunity and how these findings translate to human CAR-T cells.

title: Identification and molecular characterization of somatic mutations in MCD
text:
Brain malformations that occur during human fetal development commonly lead to severe epilepsy and
intellectual disability. In this study, we seek to identify the genetic bases of common subtypes of brain
malformations and to determine the role of implicated genes on brain development in vivo and in vitro. This
work will evaluate the role of somatic variants in brain malformations, improve the understanding of the genes
and processes involved in brain development, and will begin to illuminate strategies for early detection and
treatment options for patients suffering from these and related conditions.

title: Elucidating the functional role of KLRG1+ conventional helper T cells in the tumor microenvironment
text:
CD4+ T cells shape the tumor microenvironment to promote antitumor or pro-tumor immunity. Our data suggests
a novel, mechanistic link between KLRG1+ FoxP3- CD4+ T cells (Tconv) and both tumor progression and
immunotherapy response, yet little is known regarding the functional characteristics of this tumor-infiltrating cell
subset. The goal of this proposal is to fill this gap in knowledge by elucidating the functional, transcriptional, and
epigenetic characteristics of KLRG1+ CD4+ Tconv in cancer and determine whether novel strategies to deplete
KLRG1+ CD4+ T cells can augment antitumor immunity and enhance response to immunotherapy.

title: Identifying tissue-specific interactions to bridge mechanisms underlying muscle degeneration in Congenital Disorders of Glycosylation and Dystroglycanopathies
text:
Both Congenital Disorders of Glycosylation and dystroglycanopathies are clinically heterogenous, multisystem
disorders that can lead to severe progressive neural and muscular degeneration, which deleteriously impacts
quality of life and is frequently lethal. There are currently no cures for these diseases. We aim to leverage a
zebrafish model to gain insight into tissue-specific impacts of dpm3 expression on neuromuscular development
and provide foundational knowledge on mechanisms of disease progression in vivo.

title: Interrogation of the Impact of Selection on the Evolution of Human Pancreatic Cancer Precursor Lesions
text:
Although pancreatic cancer is a deadly disease with a dismal prognosis, it arises through non-invasive
precursor lesions that are curable if detected early enough. The goal of this project is to characterize the role of
selective forces in the evolution of precancerous pancreatic neoplasms using genomic and transcriptomic
analysis of human tissue samples and three-dimensional cultures, followed by novel computational
approaches for data integration. The results will provide critical insights into premalignant pancreatic
tumorigenesis, providing a rational foundation for the development of early detection and prevention
approaches.

title: Uncovering Personalized Circuit-Level Mechanisms for Deep Brain Stimulation in Obsessive-Compulsive Disorder
text:
Obsessive–compulsive disorder (OCD) is a severe and often treatment-resistant illness that can leave patients
with persistent, disabling symptoms despite standard therapies. This project combines advanced brain imaging
with neural recordings from surgically implanted brain electrodes to reveal how stimulating specific brain
circuits improves OCD symptoms. By identifying reliable neural features linked to symptom improvement, this
work aims to guide safer, more effective, and personalized deep brain stimulation (DBS) treatments for
patients living with the most debilitating forms of OCD.

title: Prospective natural history study of extracellular vesicle metabolimic biomarkers of myotonic dystrophy
text:
(public health relevance statement)
Myotonic dystrophy is an inherited disorder that causes progressive muscle weakness, disordered metabolism,
cardiac conduction disturbance, and cognitive dysfunction. There is no cure. The purpose of this proposal is
to develop novel strategies that will accelerate the discovery of effective treatments.

title: Advancing an inexpensive, wearable prefrontal cortex fNIRS device and integrated software for assessment of cerebral biomarkers of intoxication in real world settings
text: We propose to translate our discovery of a brain signature of acute cannabis intoxication into a tool for real world assessment of brain-based biomarkers of intoxication. The iFlexNIRS, a robust fNIRS device intended to be used like a Fitbit, will allow brain activity to be evaluated continuously and non-invasively in natural environments, accurately reflecting human experiences of intoxication across settings. iFlexNIRS will deliver high-quality connectivity and brain activation data to researchers as well as intoxication classification via an embedded machine learning classifier, providing unprecedented ecological validity for study of drug intoxication and associated cognitive impairment.

title: Pilot project to elucidate the role of DDX60L in Ebola virus disease
text:
Ebola virus causes severe disease in humans and is therefore a public health threat but understanding of the
molecular determinants of Ebola virus disease are poorly understood. This project will address the anti-Ebola
virus properties of host protein DDX60L with the goals of understanding how it modifies the outcome of infection
and identifying mechanisms that can control Ebola virus growth.

title: Vulnerabilities of MMR-deficient glioblastoma
text:
Glioblastoma is the most common and lethal brain cancer, and one key mechanism by which it develops
resistance to chemotherapy involves defects in a DNA repair pathway called mismatch repair (MMR). There are
currently no treatments proven to be effective against these especially aggressive MMR-deficient glioblastomas.
The work of this proposal investigates two new therapeutic strategies against these cancers: 1) combining
inhibitors of different calcium channels, and 2) repurposing the chemotherapy drug irinotecan and the anti-
cholesterol statin drugs as novel inhibitors of the TGF-β signaling pathway.
